labels.label: thm:main
labels.notes: Re-read against perforated.tex l.179-206, l.458-460, l.502-561 and l.679-689 (prop:starN). AbsLatticeApprox (Main.lean:654) says: for every u there are w : N -> D with val (w k) >= 0 everywhere, dirichlet (w k) <= dirichlet u, normSq_{p#}(tr (w k)) <= normSq_{p#}(tr u) on each B_j, and normSq_{p*}(val (w k)) -> normSq_{p*}(val u) (checked by #print). This is the form AUDIT-1 recommended. It is weaker than AbsLattice: AbsLattice.approx (Main.lean:661, the constant sequence through normSq_congr_abs) is kernel-checked. It is strictly weaker on the C^1 reading of OQ-93 (b). There a C^1 u that changes sign with nonzero gradient on its zero set has |u| not C^1, and a continuous w equal to |u| a.e. equals it everywhere, so AbsLattice fails. w_e = sqrt(u^2+e^2) - e with e = 1/(k+1) satisfies AbsLatticeApprox: w_e >= 0; |grad w_e| = |u|/sqrt(u^2+e^2) |grad u| <= |grad u|; tr w_e = phi_e(tr u) <= |tr u|; and w_e increases to |u|, so the p*-norm converges by monotone convergence. All quantities are finite on a compact manifold, so no junk value interferes. That argument is not formalized, and the file says so. AbsLatticeApprox is a faithful stand-in for l.458-460. The paper's step F(|u|) = F(u) on W^{1,2} implies it, the C^1 reading implies it, and it is exactly what the reduction needs: le_Fq_of_lattice passes to the limit, and the kernel checks it. It is satisfiable: toy_thm_main_hyps holds the exact form on the two-point toy model, and toy_thm_main feeds it through AbsLattice.approx. The restated theorems are no narrower than before. Main.lean was untracked and its olean rebuilt, so no pre-fix text survives on disk. I rebuilt the pre-fix forms from AUDIT-1's description: the same conclusions with hL : AbsLattice. A probe proved each one from the new theorem composed with AbsLattice.approx, and all four typecheck: thm_main with its five conjuncts written out in full, eq_main_lattice, eq_main_lattice_of_capStar_pos and le_Fq_of_lattice. The conclusions of thm_main match AUDIT-1's reading: eq:main with the printed lamMax, eq:main-asymp with mainRem, IsBigO, and the 20/7 and 5/7 bounds. thm_main_signed and thm_main_three are unchanged in substance. thm_main_three's docstring now calls it a special case at the one constant star3AtilCorr. Marks: no **`label`** anywhere in the file (ledger regex, with this paper's prefixes thm|lem|prop|cor|def|rem|q). thm:main is unmarked at char 83, as a partial row should be. thm_main's declaration docstring has lost its bold. thm_main_signed's (Main.lean:784) keeps a bold phrase without backticks, deep in the file; it is not a mark. One loose phrase, not a finding: 'thm_main with prop:starN (u >= 0) gives thm:main for every N >= 3' (SCOPE (a), REPORT question (a)). thm:main is conditional on eq:star and needs no prop:starN. The phrase is AUDIT-1's own, and its sense is true: the lattice step does not block any N under either reading.

findings.what: 'the C^1 reading satisfies it through w_e = sqrt(u^2+e^2) - e although |u| is not C^1' is stated as a plain fact. The SCOPE, the AbsLatticeApprox docstring and the hypotheses row all qualify the same statement as 'argued, not formalized'. The claim is true; I checked the argument. But a kb entry reads as house knowledge, and without the qualifier a reader would take the C^1 case as formalized somewhere.
findings.fix: Append '(argued, not formalized)' after 'although |u| is not C^1' in kb_proposals[4]. No Lean change.
